docRequirement: workflows.md:181 (§ Approve the plan before it runs): "Your permission mode controls only the launch prompt above. The subagents the workflow spawns always run in `acceptEdits` mode and inherit your tool allowlist, regardless of your session's mode. File edits are auto-approved." The floor is edits-only, not blanket: :183 keeps shell commands, web fetches and non-allowlisted MCP tools prompting mid-run, and :185 scopes the whole paragraph away from `claude -p`/Agent SDK. So a workflow-spawned child must run at an effective permission mode of at least `acceptEdits` even when the launching session is in `default`.
current: No workflow permission floor exists anywhere. `runAgent` in packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/workflow-tool.ts:560-623 builds `SpawnChildSessionArgs` with agentDef/model/effort/cwd/signal/depth/ownerTaskId/backgroundTaskId/requestedAgentId/background/hookAgentId/onAdmitted/onEvent and no permission field at all; `SpawnChildSessionArgs` (packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:24-47) has no `permissionMode` member to pass one through. The spawn goes through the same `spawnChildSession` as an ordinary subagent (`options.spawn ?? spawnChildSession`, workflow-tool.ts:466), whose child restrictions forward a mode only when the AGENT DEFINITION carries one: `...(args.agentDef.permissionMode === undefined ? {} : { permissionMode: args.agentDef.permissionMode })` (spawner.ts:575); omission means "inherit the parent's mode verbatim" (spawner.ts:328-330; packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/child-session-port.ts:44-50). Host-side the inheritance is narrow-only: packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:10406-10417 sets `childPermissionMode = record.restrictions.permissionMode ? clampPermissionModeToParent(requested, parentPermissionMode) : parentPermissionMode` and hands it to `createSession` at :10434, with the same narrow-only rule for nested ceilings at :10910-10934. Because `PERMISSION_MODE_ORDER` ranks acceptEdits(4) above default(3) (packages/shared/src/agent/mode-types.ts:63) and `clampPermissionModeToParent` returns the stricter of the two (mode-types.ts:121-131), `clamp('acceptEdits','default')` yields `'default'` — the floor is unreachable from a default-mode session even if an agent def asked for it explicitly. The consequence is live: packages/shared/src/agent/core/pre-tool-use.ts:1660-1674 enables `autoAllowFileWrites` only when `effectivePermissionMode === 'acceptEdits'`, and :1931-1949 mints a `file_write` PromptInfo for every FILE_WRITE_TOOLS call when that flag is false; the child is `hidden: true` (SessionManager.ts:10442) but its prompt is deliberately routed to the nearest visible ancestor by `permissionSurfaceRouting` (SessionManager.ts:6467-6486), so the modal reaches the human. `grep -ran acceptEdits packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/ packages/shared/src/workflows/` returns nothing (only unrelated test fixtures elsewhere in the package). The OTHER half of the same doc paragraph IS built: launch consent (packages/shared/src/workflows/workflow-launch-consent.ts; gate context at packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:708-743; `workflow_launch` prompt at pre-tool-use.ts:1534-1551) and tool-allowlist inheritance by the child session.
divergence: One missing rule, not a wrong value: workflow-spawned children take the ordinary subagent inheritance path, so their effective mode is the parent's mode, whereas the page binds them to a floor of `acceptEdits`. Only the `default` parent case actually diverges on the write axis — `auto` and `bypassPermissions` already rank above `acceptEdits`, so a floor is a no-op there. Nothing in the child spawn is even labelled as belonging to a workflow at the permission seam: `PiChildRestrictionsV1` has no workflow marker, and the only workflow signal that already reaches the host is the record's `ownerTaskId`, which a workflow run mints as `owner-workflow-<runId>` (workflow-tool.ts:460-461) versus `owner-subagent-<runId>` for a plain fan-out (packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/subagent-tool.ts:489-490) — a distinction SessionManager already parses at :2072-2074 (`isGeneratedPiOrchestrationOwnerTaskId`). Secondary, scoping-only delta: the page says "regardless of your session's mode", which would also raise a `plan`/`explore`/`dontAsk` session's workflow children into write-capable territory; that is a genuine widening of our narrow-only clamp invariant (A1) and is the one point where the fix should deviate deliberately rather than copy the sentence.

change.what: Add `export function raisePermissionModeToFloor(mode: PermissionMode, floor: PermissionMode): PermissionMode` returning the LESS strict of the two by `PERMISSION_MODE_ORDER` index (unknown mode => return `mode` unchanged). Roughly five lines. It must be a SEPARATE function — do not touch `clampPermissionModeToParent`, whose narrow-only contract is asserted by a property test over every mode pair. Carry a comment naming this as the only sanctioned widening in the system, citing workflows.md:181, and stating that its single caller is the workflow-child branch in startPiChildRuntime.
One line: add `raisePermissionModeToFloor` to the same export list so server-core can import it.

Keep the existing clamp result, then raise it for workflow children. Concretely: `const isWorkflowChild = record.restrictions.fork !== true && record.ownerTaskId?.startsWith('owner-workflow-') === true`; compute `clamped` exactly as today; then `const childPermissionMode = isWorkflowChild && isInteractiveWritePermissionMode(parentPermissionMode) ? this.normalizePiPermissionMode(raisePermissionModeToFloor(clamped, 'acceptEdits')) : clamped`. Three constraints the comment must record: (1) forks are excluded — a fork inherits the parent verbatim and the start handler already rejects a fork carrying a permissionMode (:10827); (2) the floor is gated on `isInteractiveWritePermissionMode` (mode-types.ts:98-100) so `plan`/`explore`/`dontAsk` parents keep their mode — a deliberate deviation from "regardless of your session's mode", because raising a no-write mode into a write-capable one is an escalation the clamp exists to prevent; (3) nothing else needs changing for nested agents — the raised mode becomes the child SESSION's `permissionMode` at :10434, so a grandchild's own depth-1 clamp reads the raised value and inherits it. NOTE the trust caveat: `ownerTaskId` is chosen by the Pi subprocess and `ensureOwnerTaskId` (:10654-10669) creates the task on demand, so a subagent spawn could claim the `owner-workflow-` prefix. Either accept that (the orchestrator's tool surface is host-projected and both prefixes are minted by the same trusted orchestrator code) or take the hardening entry below.

change.symbol: pre-tool-use gate context (:3842, `workflowLaunchGateContext`) — OPTIONAL hardening, only if the ownerTaskId prefix is rejected as a trust signal
change.what: The host already sees and gates the `workflow` tool call itself. Mark the parent ManagedSession 'workflow launch approved and in flight' when that gate allows the call and clear it when the tool call settles, then require that flag in addition to the `owner-workflow-` prefix in startPiChildRuntime. Two files and one boolean; do not add a field to `PiChildRestrictionsV1` for this — that interface is persisted on the session header (packages/shared/src/sessions/types.ts:397, normalized on load at packages/shared/src/sessions/jsonl.ts:95) and travels the pi-harness child-session wire, so it turns an S/M change into an L one.

Four cases: default parent + `ownerTaskId: 'owner-workflow-x'` => child session created with `acceptEdits`; default parent + `owner-subagent-x` => still `default` (the floor must not leak to plain fan-out); plan parent + workflow child => still `plan` (the recorded deviation); auto/bypass parent + workflow child => unchanged (floor is a no-op above acceptEdits).

One positive (`raise('default','acceptEdits') === 'acceptEdits'`) and one boundary (`raise('bypassPermissions','acceptEdits') === 'bypassPermissions'`, `raise('bogus' as PermissionMode,'acceptEdits') === 'bogus'`). Leave the existing narrow-only property tests at :65 and :79 untouched — they must keep passing unchanged.

blastRadius: `startPiChildRuntime` (SessionManager.ts:10391) is the single creation seam for EVERY Pi child — named subagents, conversation forks, workflow agents and plugin-hook agents (the hook-agent variant computes its own mode at :4886-4893) — so a mis-scoped condition there widens all of them; the fork exclusion is load-bearing. The narrow-only invariant it currently embodies is asserted by packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/permission-mode-clamp.test.ts (property tests over every mode pair, :65 and :79) and cross-checked by packages/server-core/src/sessions/__tests__/project-permission-mode.test.ts:35, which is why the widening must live in a new helper rather than inside `clampPermissionModeToParent`. The resulting mode crosses a PERSISTENCE boundary: it is the child session's `permissionMode` (createSession at :10434) and survives restart; `piChildRestrictions` and `childSessionState` (which carries `ownerTaskId`, written at packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.ts:127) are persisted session-header fields (packages/shared/src/sessions/types.ts:48/393/397; jsonl.ts:95 normalizes nested modes on load). Adding a field to `PiChildRestrictionsV1` would ALSO cross the pi-harness wire boundary (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/child-session-port.ts) and the start-handler validation at SessionManager.ts:10820-10934 — that is the risk trigger, and the ownerTaskId-based fix avoids it. Downstream readers of the effective mode: pre-tool-use.ts:1660-1674 and :1931-1962 (write and filesystem-command auto-approval), `shouldAllowToolInMode`, the harness runtime projection `security.permissionMode` (packages/shared/src/protocol/pi-harness-runtime.ts:192) and the renderer's mode badge for the child session — a workflow child will now report `acceptEdits` in all of them. Existing fork tests (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.fork-subagent.test.ts:86/159/183) drive `startPiChildRuntime` directly and must stay green.
userImpact: Concrete and bad on the most common setup. In the Desktop app, from a session in the DEFAULT permission mode (the shipped default), launch a workflow — the `ultracode`/keyword route, the `workflow` tool, or a saved `/<name>` — and approve the launch card. From then on every single file edit by every spawned agent raises its own approval modal in the main session (`file_write`, pre-tool-use.ts:1944-1949, routed out of the hidden child by permissionSurfaceRouting), each agent blocking until it is answered, for a run the page presents as an unattended background fan-out in the Background tasks pane. A ten-agent workflow that touches three files each is thirty modals; unanswered children sit until the spawn deadline (spawner.ts:607, default 30 min) and the run then reports errors. The user's only workaround today is to switch the session to acceptEdits or auto BEFORE launching — which the doc explicitly says should not be necessary. Latent ("none observable") for sessions already in acceptEdits, auto or bypassPermissions, and for `claude -p`-equivalent headless runs which the page exempts anyway.
